full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal arises out of the judgment and Order dated 20.05.2010 respondent. No.1 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.836 of 1991, dismissing the appeal, affirming the judgment and decree dated 28.01.1991 of the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Artha Rin Case No.123 of 1990 decreeing the case in part granting simple interest at the rate of 6% per anum from the date of filing till the date of the decree. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of this petition, in brief, are that the respondent No.1 (defendant No.1 in the Artha Rin Case) took loan of Tk.3,94,000/- under the "Power of Driving Vehicle Scheme, 1987" from the Sonali Bank Limited. Kangshanagar Branch, Comilla (plaintiff in the Artha Rin Case and petitioner herein). The loan was taken to purchase a bus and in due course the bus plied on the permitted route the respondent No. 1 duly paid the bank's installments, but could not continue to do so as the bus was not yielding sufficient income. Due to the failure of respondent No.1 to pay the loan as stipulated in the loan agreement, the petitioner filed Money Suit No. 19 of 1987 in the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Comilla for a sum of Tk.6,25,486.05, being the loan amount and accrued interest thereon. The respondent No.1 filed written statement admitting that he took the loan of Tk.3,94,000/- but denied the amount claimed by the Bank in the Money Suit. He expressed his intention to pay back the loan while explaining the reasons for his inability to pay the bank's installments in due time. At the same time he prayed that the installment may be fixed by the Court at Tk.5,000/- per month. In due course the case was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat and renumbered as Artha Rin Case No.123 of 1990. The respondent No.1, being absent when the matter was taken up for hearing, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 28.01.1991. The suit was decreed for the full claim with interest at the rate of 6% per anum from the date of filing till the date of decree. The respondent No.1 thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No.07 of 1991 with the prayer for setting aside the ex-parte decree. The petitioner filed an objection in the miscellaneous case. After hearing both the parties, by judgment and order dated 29.06.1991, the miscellaneous case was, allowed on condition that the applicants deposit Tk.50,000/- within 30 days and file the receipt in Court, failing which the application for restoration would be deemed to have been rejected. The deposit having not been made within the period stipulated by the Court, the decree was drawn up on 30.07.1991. The petitioner-Bank thereafter preferred First Appeal No.836 of 1991 claiming that the interest ordered by the trial Court at 6% per anum was too low and prayed that the interest may be ordered to be paid at 16% per anum till realization of the claimed amount. By the impugned judgment and order dated 20.05.2010 a Division Bench of the High Court Division dismissed the appeal, hence the instant leave petition. 

 3. Mr. M.A. Sobhan, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the award of interest at the rate of 6% per anum is patently illegal and interest should have been awarded at the rate of 16% per anum. He further submits that the finding of the High Court Division that waiting from 1991 till the middle of 2010 to prosecute the case showed collusion of Sonali Bank, is unwarranted and untenable. 

 5. We have considered the submissions of the learned counsel and respondent No. 1 in person and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. The High Court Division has observed that this matter has been pending since 1991 and Sonali Bank took no action to prosecute the case and if the Bank had accepted the decree when it was pronounced then by this time they would have received more money than the money which has accrued from the award of a lesser rate of interest. This is what we understand from the judgment of the High Court Division, which found no merit in the appeal.
